            if 2005 <= numeric <= 2100 and href not in plan.year_links:
                plan.year_links.append(href)

    query = urllib.parse.parse_qs(urllib.parse.urlparse(base_url).query)
    for param in ("page", "p", "pg", "start", "offset"):
        if param in query:
            plan.style = "query"
            plan.parameter = param
            try:
                plan.max_seen = max(int(v[0]) for v in [query[param]])
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                plan.max_seen = 1
            break

    if plan.style == "none" and plan.year_links:
        plan.style = "calendar"
        plan.notes.append("year links found; treating this as a calendar archive")
    elif plan.style == "none" and plan.next_links:
        plan.style = "path"
        plan.notes.append("relative next-links found; following them sequentially")
    return plan


def enumerate_pages(plan: PaginationPlan, *, max_pages: int, highest_page: int | None = None) -> list[str]:
    """Deterministic page list for one archive traversal."""
    if plan.style == "query" and plan.parameter:
        top = highest_page or plan.max_seen or 1
        urls: list[str] = []
        for page_no in range(1, top + 1):
            parts = urllib.parse.urlparse(plan.base_url)
            query = dict(urllib.parse.parse_qsl(parts.query))
            query[plan.parameter] = str(page_no)
            urls.append(urllib.parse.urlunparse(parts._replace(query=urllib.parse.urlencode(query))))
        return urls[:max_pages]
    if plan.style == "calendar" and plan.year_links:
        return plan.year_links[:max_pages]
    if plan.style == "path" and plan.next_links:
        return [plan.base_url, *plan.next_links][:max_pages]
    return [plan.base_url]


def year_url_candidates(base_url: str, years: list[int]) -> list[str]:
    """Year-suffixed candidates for sites whose charts are per-year pages."""
    parts = urllib.parse.urlparse(base_url)
    stem = parts.path.rsplit(".", 1)[0]
    ext = "." + parts.path.rsplit(".", 1)[1] if "." in parts.path else ""
    out = []
    for year in years:
        out.append(urllib.parse.urlunparse(
            parts._replace(path=f"{stem}-{year}{ext}")))
    return out


### `src/ingestion/website_discovery.py`

"""Website reconnaissance.

Answers, per source, the questions Section 5.1 of the brief asks for: is it
reachable, what does it serve, is the content server-rendered HTML or a JS
application, are there year/month archive links, is there a public JSON
endpoint, is there a downloadable file.

Everything here is observational and polite: it requests the configured entry
points at a throttled rate, honours ``robots.txt``, never submits a form, never
solves a challenge and never retries a blocked host in a tight loop. Results are
written to ``source_records`` so the report can state exactly what happened
rather than what was hoped for.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import urllib.parse
import urllib.robotparser
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

from src.core.configuration import Config, SourceSpec
from src.core.logging import get_logger
from src.core.provenance import utcnow
from src.ingestion.extraction import FetchResult, HttpClient

log = get_logger(__name__)

ARCHIVE_HINT_PATTERNS = [
    r"\d{4}", r"(jan|feb|mar|apr|may|jun|jul|aug|sep|oct|nov|dec)",
    r"record", r"chart", r"result", r"panel", r"jodi", r"archive", r"old", r"previous",
]
ASSET_EXTENSIONS = (".csv", ".xlsx", ".xls", ".json", ".zip", ".txt")


@dataclass
class PageProbe:
    url: str
    reachable: bool
    http_status: int | None
    error: str | None
    content_type: str | None = None
    byte_size: int = 0
    is_html: bool = False
    is_json: bool = False
    title: str = ""
    table_count: int = 0
    row_count: int = 0
    script_count: int = 0
    looks_js_rendered: bool = False
    status: str = "unknown"

    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "url": self.url, "reachable": self.reachable, "http_status": self.http_status,
            "error": self.error, "content_type": self.content_type,
            "byte_size": self.byte_size, "is_html": self.is_html, "is_json": self.is_json,
            "title": self.title, "table_count": self.table_count, "row_count": self.row_count,
            "script_count": self.script_count, "looks_js_rendered": self.looks_js_rendered,
            "status": self.status,
        }


@dataclass
class SourceReport:
    source_id: str
    market_id: str | None
    kind: str
    base_url: str
    reachable: bool = False
    probes: list[PageProbe] = field(default_factory=list)
    archive_links: dict[str, list[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    asset_links: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    structured_data_blocks: int = 0
    robots_allows: bool | None = None
    verdict: str = "unprobed"
    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "source_id": self.source_id, "market_id": self.market_id, "kind": self.kind,
            "base_url": self.base_url, "reachable": self.reachable,
            "robots_allows": self.robots_allows, "verdict": self.verdict,
            "structured_data_blocks": self.structured_data_blocks,
            "archive_link_groups": {k: v[:25] for k, v in self.archive_links.items()},
            "n_archive_links": sum(len(v) for v in self.archive_links.values()),
            "asset_links": self.asset_links[:40],
            "probes": [p.as_dict() for p in self.probes],
            "notes": self.notes,
        }


def _looks_js_rendered(soup: BeautifulSoup, html: str) -> bool:
    """Heuristic: almost no text, but scripts and a framework root element."""
    text = soup.get_text(" ", strip=True)
    scripts = len(soup.find_all("script"))
    framework_markers = (
        '__NEXT_DATA__', 'id="root"', 'id="app"', "ng-app", "data-reactroot",
        "vue.js", "vite", "/static/js/",
    )
    marker_hit = any(m in html for m in framework_markers)
    return (len(text) < 400 and scripts > 2) or (marker_hit and len(text) < 1500)


def probe_page(client: HttpClient, url: str) -> tuple[PageProbe, FetchResult | None]:
    result = client.get(url)
    probe = PageProbe(
        url=url,
        reachable=result.ok,
        http_status=result.status_code,
        error=result.error,
        content_type=result.content_type,
        byte_size=len(result.body or ""),
    )
    probe.status = "reachable" if result.ok else "unreachable"
    if not result.ok:
        return probe, result

    body = result.body or ""
    probe.is_html = "<html" in body[:2000].lower() or "<table" in body[:4000].lower()
    probe.is_json = body.lstrip().startswith(("{", "["))
    if probe.is_html:
        soup = BeautifulSoup(body, "lxml")
        probe.title = (soup.title.string or "").strip() if soup.title and soup.title.string else ""
        tables = soup.find_all("table")
        probe.table_count = len(tables)
        probe.row_count = sum(len(t.find_all("tr")) for t in tables)
        probe.script_count = len(soup.find_all("script"))
        probe.looks_js_rendered = _looks_js_rendered(soup, body)
        probe.status = "html_tables" if probe.table_count else "html_no_tables"
    elif probe.is_json:
        probe.status = "json"
    return probe, result


def _extract_links(base_url: str, html: str) -> tuple[dict[str, list[str]], list[str], int]:
    soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "lxml")
    archive: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    assets: list[str] = []
    for anchor in soup.find_all("a", href=True):
        href = urllib.parse.urljoin(base_url, anchor["href"])
        if not href.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
            continue
        lower = href.lower()
        if lower.endswith(ASSET_EXTENSIONS):
            if href not in assets:
                assets.append(href)
            continue
        if not any(re.search(p, lower) for p in ARCHIVE_HINT_PATTERNS):
            continue
        # Group by first path segment so the report shows archive *families*.
        path = urllib.parse.urlparse(href).path.strip("/")
        if not path:
            continue
        segments = [s for s in path.split("/") if s]
        group = "external" if urllib.parse.urlparse(href).netloc != urllib.parse.urlparse(base_url).netloc else (
            segments[0] if len(segments) > 1 else "root"
        )
        archive.setdefault(group, [])
        if href not in archive[group]:
            archive[group].append(href)
    structured = len(soup.find_all("script", type="application/ld+json"))
    return archive, assets, structured


def check_robots(client: HttpClient, base_url: str) -> bool | None:
    """Return True/False if robots.txt is readable, None if it is not."""
    robots_url = urllib.parse.urljoin(base_url, "/robots.txt")
    result = client.get(robots_url)
    if not result.ok:
        return None
    parser = urllib.robotparser.RobotFileParser()
    parser.parse(result.body.splitlines())
    try:
        return bool(parser.can_fetch(client.user_agent, base_url))
    except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - malformed robots
        return None


def investigate_source(client: HttpClient, source: SourceSpec) -> SourceReport:
    """Probe one source thoroughly enough to justify an extraction decision."""
    report = SourceReport(
        source_id=source.source_id,
        market_id=source.market_id,
        kind=source.kind,
        base_url=source.base_url,
    )
    report.robots_allows = check_robots(client, source.base_url)
    if report.robots_allows is False:
        report.verdict = "disallowed_by_robots"
        report.notes.append("robots.txt disallows fetching the base URL; no extraction attempted")
        return report

    pages = dict(source.pages)
    pages.setdefault("home", source.base_url)
    for page_name, url in pages.items():
        probe, result = probe_page(client, url)
        report.probes.append(probe)
        if result is not None and result.ok and probe.is_html:
            archive, assets, structured = _extract_links(url, result.body or "")
            for group, links in archive.items():
                existing = report.archive_links.setdefault(group, [])
                for link in links:
                    if link not in existing:
                        existing.append(link)
            report.asset_links.extend(a for a in assets if a not in report.asset_links)
            report.structured_data_blocks += structured

    report.reachable = any(p.reachable for p in report.probes)
    if not report.reachable:
        errors = {p.error for p in report.probes if p.error}
        report.verdict = "unreachable"
        report.notes.append(
            "no page could be fetched from this environment; errors observed: "
            + "; ".join(sorted(e for e in errors if e)[:4])
        )
    elif not any(p.table_count for p in report.probes):
        report.verdict = "reachable_no_tables"
        report.notes.append("pages served but no HTML tables found; content may be JS-rendered")
    else:
        report.verdict = "reachable_with_tables"
    return report


def investigate_all(config: Config, client: HttpClient | None = None) -> list[SourceReport]:
    client = client or HttpClient(config.http)
    reports: list[SourceReport] = []
    for source in config.sources.values():
        if not source.base_url:
            continue
        log.info("probing source %s (%s)", source.source_id, source.base_url)
        reports.append(investigate_source(client, source))
    return reports


def observed_at() -> str:
    return utcnow()


def summarise(reports: list[SourceReport]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "observed_at": observed_at(),
        "n_sources": len(reports),
        "n_reachable": sum(1 for r in reports if r.reachable),
        "verdicts": {r.source_id: r.verdict for r in reports},
        "observations": [r.as_dict() for r in reports],
    }


### `src/ingestion/bidding.py`

"""Market-side bidding quotes: player money, not results.

The results table records what the market *announced*. Bidding quotes record
what bookies *quoted* for each ank - the price at which they would take money.
In these markets the quote is where player psychology is priced: a low quote on
an ank means heavy public money on it (bookies pay less for it), a high quote
means the market is reluctant to take money there.

This module provides:

* a feed reader for CSV (long format) or JSON;
* an importer that upserts quotes into ``bidding_quotes`` and audits the feed
  run in ``bidding_feed_runs``;
* a pressure channel that turns quotes into side features for the forecast
  path (opt-in, exactly like the psychology channel).

**Status of the live feed:** no bidding source has ever been reachable from
this environment (the configured sites reset the TLS connection; verified
2026-11-06 and again 2026-11-09). The loader, schema, feature channel and tests
are therefore implemented and fixture-tested, but no real quotes have been
imported yet. When a feed is supplied - as a file, the same way the chart
snapshots were - ``import-bidding`` loads it and the pressure channel becomes
available to the forecast path.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date, datetime
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Mapping, Sequence

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from src.core.configuration import Config
from src.core.logging import get_logger
from src.core.provenance import utcnow
from src.storage.market_database import MarketDatabase

log = get_logger(__name__)

REQUIRED_COLUMNS = ("date", "side", "ank", "rate")


@dataclass
class BiddingImportReport:
    market_id: str
    dataset: str
    source_id: str
    source_url: str | None
    rows_read: int = 0
    inserted: int = 0
    updated: int = 0
    rejected: int = 0
    errors: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    run_id: int | None = None
    quotes_path: str | None = None

    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "market_id": self.market_id, "dataset": self.dataset,
            "source_id": self.source_id, "source_url": self.source_url,
            "rows_read": self.rows_read, "inserted": self.inserted,
            "updated": self.updated, "rejected": self.rejected,
            "errors": self.errors[:20], "run_id": self.run_id,
            "quotes_path": self.quotes_path,
        }


def _parse_row(raw: Mapping[str, Any], source: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Validate one feed row; return the canonical dict or None if malformed."""
    try:
        day = str(raw["date"]).strip()
        date.fromisoformat(day)
        side = str(raw["side"]).strip().lower()
        if side not in ("open", "close"):
            raise ValueError(f"side must be open/close, got {side!r}")
        ank = int(raw["ank"])
        if not 0 <= ank <= 9:
            raise ValueError(f"ank must be 0..9, got {ank}")
        rate = float(raw["rate"])
        if not 0 < rate <= 1:
            raise ValueError(f"rate must be in rupees (0, 1], got {rate}")
        volume = raw.get("volume")
        volume = float(volume) if volume not in (None, "", "nan") else None
        return {
            "result_date": day, "quote_side": side, "ank": ank, "rate": rate,
            "volume": volume,
        }
    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
        raise ValueError(f"{source}: {exc}") from exc


def read_feed(path: str | Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Read a bidding feed file: CSV (long format) or JSON.

    CSV expects a header with at least ``date,side,ank,rate`` and an optional
    ``volume`` column. JSON expects a list of objects with the same keys.
    """
    p = Path(path)
    text = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if p.suffix.lower() == ".json" or text.lstrip().startswith("["):
        data = json.loads(text)
        rows = [dict(item) for item in data]
    else:
        reader = csv.DictReader(text.splitlines())
        missing = set(REQUIRED_COLUMNS) - set(reader.fieldnames or [])
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(f"CSV feed missing required columns: {sorted(missing)}")
        rows = [dict(item) for item in reader]
    return [_parse_row(raw, f"row {i}") for i, raw in enumerate(rows)]


def import_bidding(config: Config, market_id: str, feed_path: str | Path, *,
                   source_id: str | None = None, source_url: str | None = None,
                   source_timestamp: str | None = None,
                   audit_dir: str | Path | None = None,
                   rebuild: bool = False) -> BiddingImportReport:
    """Load a bidding feed for one market into ``bidding_quotes``."""
    if config.dataset.name != "live":
        raise ValueError("bidding quotes are real-world data and may only be loaded "
                         "into the live dataset, not into a control world")
    config.market(market_id)
    market = config.market(market_id)
    source = source_id or str(market.primary_source) + "_bidding"

    rows = read_feed(feed_path)
    report = BiddingImportReport(market_id=market_id, dataset=config.dataset.name,
                                 source_id=source, source_url=source_url,
                                 rows_read=len(rows))
    if not rows:
        return report

    db = MarketDatabase(config, market_id)
    db.manager.initialise(market_id, rebuild=rebuild)

    # Distinguish new quotes from revised ones for the report.
    with db.session(read_only=True) as conn:
        existing = {
            (r["result_date"], r["quote_side"], r["ank"])
            for r in conn.execute(
                "SELECT result_date, quote_side, ank FROM bidding_quotes")
        }

    payload = {
        "source_id": source, "source_url": source_url,
        "source_timestamp": source_timestamp,
    }
    rows = [{**row, "source_id": source, "source_url": source_url,
             "source_timestamp": source_timestamp,
             "extraction_timestamp": utcnow(),
             "raw_payload": json.dumps(payload),
             "notes": None}
            for row in rows]
    n = db.save_bidding_quotes(rows)
    report.inserted = sum(1 for r in rows
                          if (r["result_date"], r["quote_side"], r["ank"]) not in existing)
    report.updated = n - report.inserted

    with db.session() as conn:
        cur = conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO bidding_feed_runs (market_id, source_id, source_url, "
            "started_at, finished_at, rows_read, rows_inserted, rows_updated, "
            "rows_rejected, notes) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (market_id, source, source_url, utcnow(), utcnow(),
             report.rows_read, report.inserted, report.updated, report.rejected,
             "feed imported; quotes upserted"),
        )
        report.run_id = int(cur.lastrowid)

    if audit_dir is not None:
        out = Path(audit_dir)
        out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        report.quotes_path = str(out / f"bidding_import_{market_id}.json")
        Path(report.quotes_path).write_text(
            json.dumps(report.as_dict(), indent=2, default=str))
    return report


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# pressure channel (side features for the forecast path)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def bidding_pressure_features(quotes: pd.DataFrame,
                              dates: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Turn quoted rates into a pressure channel, aligned to ``dates``.

    ``quotes`` is the ``bidding_quotes`` frame (or an equivalent with columns
    ``result_date, quote_side, ank, rate``). The channel is *inverse rate*:
    the lower the quote on an ank, the more money the market expects on it.

    Produces 20 per-ank columns (``bid_press_{side}_{ank}``), the per-side
    entropy of the pressure distribution, and the overall max pressure - all
    NaN for dates with no quotes. This is a *side backup* channel: it is added
    only when a feed exists and the caller opts in; it never replaces the
    results-based features.
    """
    dates = pd.DatetimeIndex(dates)
    out = pd.DataFrame(index=dates)
    if quotes is None or quotes.empty:
        for side in ("open", "close"):
            for ank in range(10):
                out[f"bid_press_{side}_{ank}"] = np.nan
        return out

    q = quotes.copy()
    q["result_date"] = pd.to_datetime(q["result_date"])
    q["press"] = 1.0 / q["rate"] - 1.0
    for side in ("open", "close"):
        sub = q[q["quote_side"] == side]
        pivot = sub.pivot_table(index="result_date", columns="ank",
                                values="press", aggfunc="mean")
        for ank in range(10):
            col = f"bid_press_{side}_{ank}"
            out[col] = pivot[ank].reindex(dates).to_numpy() if ank in pivot.columns \
                else np.nan
        present = pivot.notna().any(axis=1).reindex(dates).fillna(False)
        p = pivot.reindex(dates)
        entropy = pd.Series(
            -np.sum(np.where(p > 0, p * np.log(np.clip(p, 1e-12, None)), 0.0),
                    axis=1),
            index=dates)
        out[f"bid_entropy_{side}"] = entropy.where(present)
        out[f"bid_max_{side}"] = p.max(axis=1).where(present)
    return out


### `src/ingestion/synthetic_control.py`

"""Synthetic control datasets - the substitute for data this environment cannot fetch.

WHY THIS EXISTS
---------------
The source hosts are unreachable from the build sandbox (egress is restricted to
a small allowlist; every attempt returns ``SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL``). The scientific
rules forbid inventing market history, so instead of a fake "Kalyan" dataset we
generate two explicitly-synthetic worlds with *known* data-generating processes:

``synthetic_null`` (H0)
    Draws are i.i.d. uniform on 0-9, markets independent. There is nothing to
    find. A correctly-built research platform must conclude "no predictive
    information" - and if it instead reports a discovery, the platform is broken.

``synthetic_signal`` (H1)
    Draws follow a first-order Markov chain with a known transition matrix, and
    Main Bazar's close has a weak, publication-order-respecting dependence on
    Kalyan's same-day open. The platform must detect *some* of this out of sample.

Together they are a two-sided calibration test of the whole pipeline: a false
positive rate that is honest, and a power that is non-zero. Every row written by
this module is stamped ``synthetic_control`` and lives under a separate database
tree, so it can never be reported as market data.

The generator is seeded and its parameters are recorded in the manifest, so the
controls are exactly reproducible.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, timedelta
from typing import Any

import numpy as np

from src.core.configuration import Config
from src.core.logging import get_logger
from src.core.provenance import ExtractionLedger, content_hash, utcnow
from src.storage.market_database import MarketDatabase

log = get_logger(__name__)

SYNTHETIC_STATUS = "synthetic_control"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ControlSpec:
    """The data-generating process, stated explicitly so it can be audited."""

    name: str
    start: date
    end: date
    # Persistence weight: 0 -> i.i.d. uniform; >0 -> mass moved to (previous + 1) % 10
    open_persistence: float
    close_persistence: float
    marginal_tilt: float
    # Main Bazar close depends on Kalyan's same-day open by this much.
    cross_market_strength: float
    seed: int

    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "name": self.name,
            "start": self.start.isoformat(),
            "end": self.end.isoformat(),
            "open_persistence": self.open_persistence,
            "marginal_tilt": self.marginal_tilt,
            "close_persistence": self.close_persistence,
            "cross_market_strength": self.cross_market_strength,
            "seed": self.seed,
            "distribution": "categorical over 0-9",
            "draw_calendar": "Mon-Sat (Sunday excluded)",
        }


NULL_SPEC = ControlSpec(
    name="synthetic_null", start=date(2016, 1, 1), end=date(2025, 12, 31),
    open_persistence=0.0, close_persistence=0.0, marginal_tilt=0.0,
    cross_market_strength=0.0, seed=20250101,
)

SIGNAL_SPEC = ControlSpec(
    name="synthetic_signal", start=date(2016, 1, 1), end=date(2025, 12, 31),
    open_persistence=0.30, close_persistence=0.22, marginal_tilt=0.12,
    cross_market_strength=0.18, seed=20250101,
)


def trading_days(start: date, end: date) -> list[date]:
    """Mon-Sat calendar; these markets do not draw on Sunday."""
    days: list[date] = []
    cursor = start
    while cursor <= end:
        if cursor.weekday() != 6:
            days.append(cursor)
        cursor += timedelta(days=1)
    return days


def _transition_matrix(rng: np.random.Generator, persistence: float,
                       tilt: float = 0.0) -> np.ndarray:
    """Base(1/K) mass plus ``persistence`` mass on the successor state.

    The successor is ``(state + 1) % 10`` rather than the state itself, because
    pure self-persistence is trivially detectable and would overstate the power
    test. The remaining mass is spread unevenly (a mild preference profile) so
    the marginal is deliberately *not* perfectly uniform - which also exercises
    the frequency-based methods.
    """
    k = 10
    base = np.full((k, k), (1.0 - persistence) / k)
    for i in range(k):
        base[i, (i + 1) % k] += persistence
    # Optional deterministic preference structure. The H0 world must be exactly
    # uniform, so tilt is 0 there; only the H1 world carries a mild imbalance.
    preference = 1.0 + tilt * np.cos(2 * np.pi * np.arange(k) / k * 2)
    base = base * preference[None, :]
    return base / base.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)


def _sample_chain(rng: np.random.Generator, n: int, matrix: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    states = np.empty(n, dtype=int)
    states[0] = rng.integers(0, matrix.shape[0])
    cumulative = np.cumsum(matrix, axis=1)
    for t in range(1, n):
        u = rng.random()
        states[t] = int(np.searchsorted(cumulative[states[t - 1]], u))
    return states


def _panna_for_ank(rng: np.random.Generator, ank: int) -> str:
    """A 3-digit panel whose digit sum mod 10 equals ``ank`` (as the real charts do)."""
    digits = rng.integers(0, 10, size=3)
    current = int(digits.sum() % 10)
    if current != ank:
        # Adjust the last digit - always possible for a modulus of 10.
        digits[2] = (digits[2] + (ank - current)) % 10
    return "".join(str(int(d)) for d in digits)


def generate(spec: ControlSpec) -> dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    """Build the result rows for both markets under ``spec``."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(spec.seed)
    days = trading_days(spec.start, spec.end)
    n = len(days)

    open_matrix = _transition_matrix(rng, spec.open_persistence, spec.marginal_tilt)
    close_matrix = _transition_matrix(rng, spec.close_persistence, spec.marginal_tilt)

    kalyan_open = _sample_chain(rng, n, open_matrix)
    kalyan_close = _sample_chain(rng, n, close_matrix)

    if spec.cross_market_strength > 0:
        # Main Bazar's Open follows the same process; its Close is a mixture of
        # its own chain and Kalyan's *earlier-published* same-day Open.
        mb_open = _sample_chain(rng, n, open_matrix)
        mb_close_own = _sample_chain(rng, n, close_matrix)
        shift = spec.cross_market_strength
        mb_close = np.array([
            kalyan_open[t] if rng.random() < shift else mb_close_own[t]
            for t in range(n)
        ])
    else:
        mb_open = _sample_chain(rng, n, open_matrix)
        mb_close = _sample_chain(rng, n, close_matrix)

    out: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {"kalyan": [], "main_bazar": []}
    for market_id, open_seq, close_seq in (
        ("kalyan", kalyan_open, kalyan_close),
        ("main_bazar", mb_open, mb_close),
    ):
        for idx, day in enumerate(days):
            o_ank = int(open_seq[idx])
            c_ank = int(close_seq[idx])
            out[market_id].append({
                "market_id": market_id,
                "result_date": day.isoformat(),
                "open_panna": _panna_for_ank(rng, o_ank),
                "open_ank": o_ank,
                "close_panna": _panna_for_ank(rng, c_ank),
                "close_ank": c_ank,
                "jodi": f"{o_ank}{c_ank}",
                "source_id": "synthetic_generator",
                "source_url": None,
                "source_timestamp": None,
                "extraction_timestamp": utcnow(),
                "verification_status": SYNTHETIC_STATUS,
                "raw_payload": {"generator": "src.ingestion.synthetic_control",
                                "spec": spec.as_dict()},
                "notes": f"{spec.name}: controlled DGP, not market data",
            })
    return out


def build_dataset(config: Config, spec: ControlSpec, *, rebuild: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Materialise one control dataset into its own database tree."""
    if config.dataset.name != spec.name:
        raise ValueError(
            f"config dataset is '{config.dataset.name}' but spec is '{spec.name}'; "
            "refusing to mix control worlds"
        )
    log.info("generating control dataset %s (%s..%s)", spec.name, spec.start, spec.end)
    frames = generate(spec)
    summary: dict[str, Any] = {"spec": spec.as_dict(), "markets": {}}
    for market_id, rows in frames.items():
        config.database_path(market_id).unlink(missing_ok=True)
        db = MarketDatabase(config, market_id)
        db.manager.initialise(market_id)
        outcome = db.upsert_results(rows)
        record_generation_provenance(config, market_id, spec, n_rows=len(rows),
                                     inserted=outcome.inserted)
        db.record_update("synthetic_generation", "ok", utcnow(),
                         new_records=outcome.inserted, new_watermark=rows[-1]["result_date"])
        summary["markets"][market_id] = {
            "generated": len(rows), "inserted": outcome.inserted,
            "rejected": outcome.rejected, "errors": outcome.errors[:5],
            "oldest": rows[0]["result_date"], "newest": rows[-1]["result_date"],
        }
        log.info("%s: %d rows generated, %d inserted, %d rejected",
                 market_id, len(rows), outcome.inserted, outcome.rejected)
    summary["generated_at"] = utcnow()
    return summary


def record_generation_provenance(config: Config, market_id: str, spec: ControlSpec, *,
                                 n_rows: int, inserted: int | None = None,
                                 when: str | None = None) -> int | None:
    """Write the generation act into `extraction_runs` / `source_records`.

    The provenance tables exist so every number in a database can be traced to the
    act that produced it. For a control dataset that act is *generation*, not
    fetching, and it is recorded as such: one run per market and one source record
    whose URL is `synthetic://<dataset>/<market>` and whose notes carry the seed and
    the full generator parameters. Idempotent: a market that already has a
    successful `synthetic_generator` run is not recorded twice.
    """
    db = MarketDatabase(config, market_id)
    url = f"synthetic://{spec.name}/{market_id}"
    notes = (
        f"seed={spec.seed} start={spec.start.isoformat()} end={spec.end.isoformat()} "
        f"open_persistence={spec.open_persistence} close_persistence={spec.close_persistence} "
        f"marginal_tilt={spec.marginal_tilt} cross_market_strength={spec.cross_market_strength} "
        f"generated_by=src.ingestion.synthetic_control.generate"
    )
    with db.session() as conn:
        # Idempotent on the *content* of the record, not just on the source id:
        # a second backfill of the same spec must not append a second run.
        existing = conn.execute(
            "SELECT r.run_id FROM extraction_runs r "
            "JOIN source_records s ON s.run_id = r.run_id "
            "WHERE r.market_id = ? AND r.source_id = ? AND r.status = 'ok' AND s.notes = ? "
            "ORDER BY r.run_id DESC LIMIT 1",
            (market_id, "synthetic_generator", notes),
        ).fetchone()
        if existing is not None:
            return None
        with ExtractionLedger(conn, market_id, "synthetic_generator",
                              config.fingerprint()) as run:
            run.record_page(url, None, True, byte_size=0, parse_status="generated",
                            notes=notes, body=notes)
            run.finish("ok", pages_requested=1, pages_ok=1, pages_failed=0,
                       records_seen=n_rows, records_inserted=int(inserted or n_rows),
                       records_revised=0,
                       error_text="" if when is None else f"backfilled_at={utcnow()} original={when}")
            return run.run_id


---

## Preprocessing

### `src/preprocessing/cleaning.py`

"""Cleaning: turn stored rows into a validated, chronologically ordered table.

Cleaning never deletes a record to make an analysis work. It *flags*. The rules
are:

* rows are sorted by date and must be unique per date (the schema enforces this;
  cleaning verifies it and fails loudly if the invariant is broken);
* a row missing the target component is excluded from that target's series only,
  and the exclusion is counted and reported;
* values are re-validated against their declared outcome space;
* nothing is imputed. A missing draw stays missing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

import pandas as pd

from src.core.configuration import Config
from src.core.logging import get_logger
from src.core.validation import ValidationError, validate_result_value
from src.storage.market_database import MarketDatabase

log = get_logger(__name__)


@dataclass
class CleanResult:
    market_id: str
    target: str
    frame: pd.DataFrame
    n_raw: int = 0
    n_used: int = 0
    n_missing_target: int = 0
    n_invalid: int = 0
    exclusions: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
    dataset: str = "live"

    def summary(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "market_id": self.market_id, "target": self.target,
            "n_raw": self.n_raw, "n_used": self.n_used,
            "n_missing_target": self.n_missing_target, "n_invalid": self.n_invalid,
            "first_date": (self.frame["result_date"].min().date().isoformat()
                           if not self.frame.empty else None),
            "last_date": (self.frame["result_date"].max().date().isoformat()
                          if not self.frame.empty else None),
            "dataset": self.dataset,
        }


def clean_results(config: Config, market_id: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Load and validate one market's active result history."""
    db = MarketDatabase(config, market_id)
    market = config.market(market_id)
    df = db.results()
    if df.empty:
        return df

    df = df.sort_values("result_date").reset_index(drop=True)
    dups = df["result_date"].duplicated()
    if dups.any():
        raise ValidationError(
            f"{market_id}: duplicate active result dates {df.loc[dups, 'result_date'].tolist()[:5]}"
        )

    for column, space in (("open_panna", "panna"), ("close_panna", "panna"),
                          ("open_ank", "ank"), ("close_ank", "ank"), ("jodi", "jodi")):
        if column not in df:
            continue
        cleaned = []
        for value in df[column]:
            if pd.isna(value):
                cleaned.append(None)
                continue
            try:
                cleaned.append(validate_result_value(value, space))
            except ValidationError:
                log.warning("%s: invalid %s value %r -> nulled", market_id, column, value)
                cleaned.append(None)
        df[column + "_c"] = cleaned
        df[column] = cleaned
        df.drop(columns=[column + "_c"], inplace=True)

    # Consistency: ank must equal digit sum of panna when both are present.
    # A panna may legitimately be missing while its ank is known (the jodi carries
    # both anks), and pandas turns those NULLs into NaN, so the guard is `isna`,
    # not `is None`.
    if {"open_panna", "open_ank"} <= set(df.columns):
        derived = df["open_panna"].map(
            lambda p: None if pd.isna(p) else sum(int(c) for c in str(p)) % 10
        )
        mismatch = (derived.notna() & df["open_ank"].notna() & (derived != df["open_ank"]))
        if mismatch.any():
            log.warning("%s: %d open panna/ank mismatches (kept as reported)",
                        market_id, int(mismatch.sum()))
            df.loc[mismatch, "open_ank"] = derived[mismatch]

    if "open_ank" in df and "close_ank" in df and "jodi" in df:
        expected = df.apply(
            lambda r: None if pd.isna(r["open_ank"]) or pd.isna(r["close_ank"])
            else f"{int(r['open_ank'])}{int(r['close_ank'])}",
            axis=1,
        )
        bad = expected.notna() & df["jodi"].notna() & (expected.astype(str) != df["jodi"].astype(str))
        if bad.any():
            log.warning("%s: %d jodi/open-close mismatches; trusting open+close",
                        market_id, int(bad.sum()))
            df.loc[bad, "jodi"] = expected[bad]

    df.attrs["market_id"] = market.market_id
    df.attrs["dataset"] = config.dataset.name
    return df


def clean_target(config: Config, market_id: str, target: str) -> CleanResult:
    """Produce the ordered outcome series for one target, with exclusion accounting."""
    market = config.market(market_id)
    spec = market.target(target)
    df = clean_results(config, market_id)
    if df.empty:
        return CleanResult(market_id=market.market_id, target=target,
                           frame=df, dataset=config.dataset.name)

    column = spec.field
    n_raw = len(df)
    missing = df[column].isna()
    used = df.loc[~missing].copy()
    used = used.sort_values("result_date").reset_index(drop=True)

    if spec.space == "ank":
        used["y"] = used[column].astype(int)
    elif spec.space == "jodi":
        used["y"] = used[column].astype(str).str.zfill(2)
    else:
        used["y"] = used[column].astype(str)

    return CleanResult(
        market_id=market.market_id, target=target, frame=used,
        n_raw=n_raw, n_used=len(used), n_missing_target=int(missing.sum()),
        exclusions=[
            {"date": d.date().isoformat(), "reason": f"missing {column}"}
            for d in df.loc[missing, "result_date"].head(50)
        ],
        dataset=config.dataset.name,
    )


def outcome_series(config: Config, market_id: str, target: str) -> pd.Series:
    """Convenience: date-indexed outcome series, no missing values."""
    result = clean_target(config, market_id, target)
    if result.frame.empty:
        return pd.Series(dtype="object", name=target)
    return result.frame.set_index("result_date")["y"].rename(target)


### `src/preprocessing/feature_engineering.py`

"""Causal feature construction.

THE ONE RULE: every feature for the draw on date ``t`` is computed from
information available strictly before ``t`` - plus, for the *close* target only,
the same day's *open*, which these markets publish first.

The implementation enforces this structurally rather than by review: all
quantities are produced by shifting the outcome series before any rolling or
expanding computation touches it. :func:`verify_causality` then re-derives every
feature column from scratch on truncated history and asserts equality, which is
a genuine leakage test rather than a comment.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import warnings
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Sequence

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from src.core.logging import get_logger
from src.preprocessing.normalization import ANK_SUPPORT
from src.preprocessing.psychology import PsychologyConfig, psychology_features

log = get_logger(__name__)

FEATURE_VERSION = "feat-v1"
K_ANK = len(ANK_SUPPORT)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FeatureConfig:
    windows: tuple[int, ...] = (25, 50, 100, 250)
    ewm_lambdas: tuple[float, ...] = (0.95, 0.99)
    max_gap_features: bool = True
    include_transition_row: bool = True
    include_calendar: bool = True
    include_same_day_open: bool = True
    include_cross_market: bool = True
    #: Admit a *same-day* foreign Open for Close targets, but only where
    #: markets.yaml explicitly declares that the foreign Open is published first.
    include_cross_same_day_open: bool = True
    #: Side channel: player-psychology proxies (recent heat, cold streaks,
    #: coverage). Off by default so existing results stay reproducible; on
    #: only when a run explicitly asks for it.
    include_psychology: bool = False
    psychology: "PsychologyConfig" = field(default_factory=lambda: PsychologyConfig())
    feature_version: str = FEATURE_VERSION


def _expanding_freq(y: np.ndarray, k: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """p_k(t) estimated from rows 0..t-1 inclusive (causal: y is pre-shifted)."""
    n = len(y)
    out = np.full((n, k), np.nan)
    counts = np.zeros(k)
    for t in range(n):
        total = counts.sum()
        if total > 0:
            out[t] = counts / total
        if y[t] >= 0:
            counts[y[t]] += 1
    return out


def _rolling_freq(y: np.ndarray, k: int, window: int) -> np.ndarray:
    n = len(y)
    out = np.full((n, k), np.nan)
    counts = np.zeros(k)
    for t in range(n):
        total = counts.sum()
        if total > 0:
            out[t] = counts / total
        if y[t] >= 0:
            counts[y[t]] += 1
            if t - window >= 0 and y[t - window] >= 0:
                counts[y[t - window]] -= 1
    return out


def _ewm_freq(y: np.ndarray, k: int, lam: float) -> np.ndarray:
    n = len(y)
    out = np.full((n, k), np.nan)
    weights = np.zeros(k)
    for t in range(n):
        total = weights.sum()
        if total > 0:
            out[t] = weights / total
        weights *= lam
        if y[t] >= 0:
            weights[y[t]] += 1.0
    return out


def _gap_features(y: np.ndarray, k: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Observations elapsed since each category was last seen (capped at 999)."""
    n = len(y)
    last_seen = np.full(k, -1)
    out = np.full((n, k), np.nan)
    for t in range(n):
        for c in range(k):
            out[t, c] = 999.0 if last_seen[c] < 0 else float(t - last_seen[c])
        if y[t] >= 0:
            last_seen[y[t]] = t
    return out


def _transition_rows(y: np.ndarray, k: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Row of the causal first-order transition matrix for the most recent state."""
    n = len(y)
    out = np.full((n, k), np.nan)
    counts = np.zeros((k, k))
    rows = np.zeros(k)
    last = -1
    for t in range(n):
        if last >= 0 and rows[last] > 0:
            out[t] = counts[last] / rows[last]
        if y[t] >= 0:
            if last >= 0:
                counts[last, y[t]] += 1.0
                rows[last] += 1.0
            last = y[t]
    return out


def build_features(
    y: np.ndarray,
    cfg: FeatureConfig,
    *,
    same_day_open: np.ndarray | None = None,
    cross_open: np.ndarray | None = None,
    cross_close: np.ndarray | None = None,
    dates: pd.DatetimeIndex | None = None,
    cross_open_today: np.ndarray | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Build the causal feature matrix.

    ``y`` is the integer-coded target sequence. A value of ``-1`` marks an
    unknown outcome and is treated as "no information" rather than as a class.

    ``same_day_open`` is only supplied for the *close* target, where the open is
    published earlier the same day. It is inserted unshifted on purpose; the
    caller is responsible for only passing it when that is genuinely true.
    """
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=int)
    n = len(y)
    k = K_ANK
    cols: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}

    # Everything below is computed on the *own* history and then shifted by one,
    # which is what makes it causal.
    shifted = np.concatenate([[-1], y[:-1]])

    expanding = _expanding_freq(shifted, k)
    for c in range(k):
        cols[f"freq_all_{c}"] = expanding[:, c] - 1.0 / k

    for window in cfg.windows:
        freq = _rolling_freq(shifted, k, window)
        # Compact representation: keep the window's overall dispersion plus the
        # top-3 categories' excess probability, rather than 10 more columns each.
        for c in range(k):
            if window in (25, 100):
                cols[f"freq_w{window}_{c}"] = freq[:, c] - 1.0 / k
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
            cols[f"freq_w{window}_max_excess"] = np.nanmax(freq - 1.0 / k, axis=1)

    for lam in cfg.ewm_lambdas:
        ewm = _ewm_freq(shifted, k, lam)
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
            cols[f"ewm_{str(lam).replace('.', '')}_max_excess"] = np.nanmax(ewm - 1.0 / k, axis=1)
        cols[f"ewm_{str(lam).replace('.', '')}_entropy"] = -np.nansum(
            np.where(ewm > 0, ewm * np.log2(np.clip(ewm, 1e-12, None)), 0.0), axis=1
        )

    if cfg.max_gap_features:
        gaps = _gap_features(shifted, k)
        for c in range(k):
            cols[f"gap_{c}"] = gaps[:, c]
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
            cols["min_gap"] = np.nanmin(gaps, axis=1)

    if cfg.include_transition_row:
        trans = _transition_rows(shifted, k)
        for c in range(k):
            cols[f"trans_{c}"] = trans[:, c] - 1.0 / k

    # Player-psychology side channel (opt-in). Same shifted history, so the
    # causality of every column is inherited from the shifted series.
    if cfg.include_psychology:
        psy = psychology_features(shifted, cfg.psychology)
        for col in psy.columns:
            cols[col] = psy[col].to_numpy()

    # Scalar summaries of the latest outcome (already shifted => previous draw).
    prev = np.concatenate([[np.nan], y[:-1]]).astype(float)
    cols["prev_value"] = prev
    cols["prev_parity"] = np.mod(prev, 2)
    cols["prev_mod5"] = np.mod(prev, 5)
    cols["prev_is_high"] = (prev >= 5).astype(float)
    cols["prev_digital_root"] = np.where(
        np.isnan(prev), np.nan, np.mod(np.mod(prev - 1, 9) + 1, 10) if False else np.mod(prev, 10)
    )
    running = pd.Series(prev).rolling(10, min_periods=1).mean().to_numpy()
    cols["prev_mean10"] = running

    # Availability count = how much training data exists at this row.
    cols["history_size"] = np.arange(n, dtype=float)

    # Same-day open (close target only).
    if same_day_open is not None and cfg.include_same_day_open:
        o = np.asarray(same_day_open, dtype=float)
        cols["open_today"] = o
        cols["open_today_parity"] = np.mod(o, 2)
        cols["open_today_is_high"] = (o >= 5).astype(float)
        cols["open_today_gap_min"] = np.nanmin(_gap_features(
            np.where(np.isnan(o), -1, o).astype(int), k), axis=1)

    # Cross-market features: previous day's published values only.
    if cross_open is not None and cfg.include_cross_market:
        co = np.asarray(cross_open, dtype=float)
        cols["x_prev_open"] = np.concatenate([[np.nan], co[:-1]])
    if cross_close is not None and cfg.include_cross_market:
        cc = np.asarray(cross_close, dtype=float)
        cols["x_prev_close"] = np.concatenate([[np.nan], cc[:-1]])
        cols["x_prev_jodi_sum"] = np.mod(cols["x_prev_open"] + cols["x_prev_close"], 10)

    # Same-day foreign Open (Close targets only). Admitted only when the
    # configuration declares that the partner market publishes its Open before
    # this market closes; see markets.yaml -> cross_open_precedence.
    if cross_open_today is not None and cfg.include_cross_same_day_open:
        xo = np.asarray(cross_open_today, dtype=float)
        cols["x_today_open"] = xo
        cols["x_today_open_parity"] = np.mod(xo, 2)
        cols["x_today_open_is_high"] = (xo >= 5).astype(float)

    if cfg.include_calendar and dates is not None:
        dow = pd.DatetimeIndex(dates).dayofweek.to_numpy().astype(float)
        cols["dow_sin"] = np.sin(2 * np.pi * dow / 7)
        cols["dow_cos"] = np.cos(2 * np.pi * dow / 7)
        cols["dom"] = pd.DatetimeIndex(dates).day.to_numpy().astype(float)
        cols["month"] = pd.DatetimeIndex(dates).month.to_numpy().astype(float)

    frame = pd.DataFrame(cols)
    frame = frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return frame


def verify_causality(
    y: np.ndarray,
    cfg: FeatureConfig,
    *,
    same_day_open: np.ndarray | None = None,
    cross_open: np.ndarray | None = None,
    cross_close: np.ndarray | None = None,
    dates: pd.DatetimeIndex | None = None,
    cross_open_today: np.ndarray | None = None,
    n_checks: int = 5,
) -> dict:
    """Rebuild features on truncated history and assert the prefix is identical.

    If any feature for row ``t`` had used data from row ``t`` or later, the value
    computed with only ``0..cut`` available would differ from the full-history
    value. This catches look-ahead bias empirically instead of trusting review.
    """
    full = build_features(y, cfg, same_day_open=same_day_open, cross_open=cross_open,
                          cross_close=cross_close, dates=dates,
                          cross_open_today=cross_open_today)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
    n = len(y)
    cuts = sorted({int(c) for c in rng.integers(30, max(31, n - 1), size=n_checks)})
    mismatches: list[dict] = []
    for cut in cuts:
        truncated = build_features(
            y[: cut + 1], cfg,
            same_day_open=None if same_day_open is None else same_day_open[: cut + 1],
            cross_open=None if cross_open is None else cross_open[: cut + 1],
            cross_close=None if cross_close is None else cross_close[: cut + 1],
            dates=None if dates is None else dates[: cut + 1],
            cross_open_today=(None if cross_open_today is None
                              else cross_open_today[: cut + 1]),
        )
        common = [c for c in full.columns if c in truncated.columns]
        a = full.loc[: cut, common].to_numpy(dtype=float)
        b = truncated.loc[: cut, common].to_numpy(dtype=float)
        same = np.allclose(a, b, equal_nan=True, rtol=1e-9, atol=1e-9)
        if not same:
            bad_cols = [
                col for i, col in enumerate(common)
                if not np.allclose(a[:, i], b[:, i], equal_nan=True, rtol=1e-9, atol=1e-9)
            ]
            mismatches.append({"cut": cut, "columns": bad_cols[:8]})
    return {
        "checked_cuts": len(cuts),
        "leaks_found": len(mismatches),
        "details": mismatches[:5],
        "passed": not mismatches,
        "feature_count": int(full.shape[1]),
        "feature_version": cfg.feature_version,
    }


def finite_matrix(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> np.ndarray:
    """Model-ready float matrix: NaN/inf -> 0 after the warm-up rows are dropped.

    Rows in the warm-up window (where expanding statistics are undefined) are the
    responsibility of the caller - :func:`walk_forward_matrices` drops them.
    """
    return frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float)


def feature_names(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> list[str]:
    return list(frame.columns)


### `src/preprocessing/normalization.py`

"""Transformations between the representations matka results use.

Three representations of the same draw coexist, and confusing them is the single
easiest way to corrupt an analysis:

``panna``  the 3-digit panel, e.g. ``"128"`` - a fixed-width *string*
``ank``    the single digit, ``digit_sum(panna) % 10`` - an *integer* 0-9
``jodi``   the concatenation ``f"{open_ank}{close_ank}"`` - a fixed-width *string*

``"07"`` is a valid jodi and is not the integer 7. ``"128"`` is not the integer
128. These functions are the only sanctioned conversions, and they preserve
width and type.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Iterable, Sequence

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from src.core.validation import ValidationError

ANK_SUPPORT: tuple[int, ...] = tuple(range(10))
JODI_SUPPORT: tuple[str, ...] = tuple(f"{i:02d}" for i in range(100))
PANNA_SUPPORT: tuple[str, ...] = tuple(f"{i:03d}" for i in range(1000))


def support_for(space: str) -> tuple:
    if space == "ank":
        return ANK_SUPPORT
    if space == "jodi":
        return JODI_SUPPORT
    if space == "panna":
        return PANNA_SUPPORT
    raise ValidationError(f"unknown outcome space: {space}")


def panna_to_ank(panna: str | int) -> int:
    """Digit-sum-mod-10. Rejects values that are not exactly 3 digits."""
    text = str(panna).strip()
    if len(text) != 3 or not text.isdigit():
        raise ValidationError(f"panna must be a 3-digit string, got {panna!r}")
    return int(sum(int(c) for c in text) % 10)


def anks_to_jodi(open_ank: int, close_ank: int) -> str:
    if not (0 <= int(open_ank) <= 9 and 0 <= int(close_ank) <= 9):
        raise ValidationError(f"ank out of range: {open_ank!r}, {close_ank!r}")
    return f"{int(open_ank)}{int(close_ank)}"


def jodi_to_anks(jodi: str | int) -> tuple[int, int]:
    text = str(jodi).strip().zfill(2)
    if len(text) != 2 or not text.isdigit():
        raise ValidationError(f"jodi must be 2 digits, got {jodi!r}")
    return int(text[0]), int(text[1])


def digits_of(panna: str | int) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    text = str(panna).strip()
    if len(text) != 3 or not text.isdigit():
        raise ValidationError(f"panna must be 3 digits, got {panna!r}")
    return int(text[0]), int(text[1]), int(text[2])


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# encodings
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def encode_categorical(values: Sequence, support: Sequence) -> np.ndarray:
    """Map labels to 0..K-1 indices, raising on anything unseen."""
    lookup = {str(v): i for i, v in enumerate(support)}
    out = np.empty(len(values), dtype=int)
    for idx, value in enumerate(values):
        key = str(value)
        if key not in lookup:
            raise ValidationError(f"value {value!r} not in declared support")
        out[idx] = lookup[key]
    return out


def one_hot(indices: np.ndarray, k: int) -> np.ndarray:
    out = np.zeros((len(indices), k), dtype=float)
    out[np.arange(len(indices)), np.asarray(indices, dtype=int)] = 1.0
    return out


def numeric_encoding(series: pd.Series, space: str) -> pd.Series:
    """A *meaningful* numeric view of a categorical series.

    For ``ank`` the digit itself is meaningful (0-9 on a line). For ``jodi`` the
    encoded value 0-99 is an arbitrary label and must not be modelled as a
    magnitude - :func:`has_defensible_numeric_representation` says so explicitly,
    and the time-series methods check it before running.
    """
    if space == "ank":
        return pd.to_numeric(series, errors="coerce").astype(float)
    raise ValidationError(
        f"outcome space '{space}' has no defensible numeric representation; "
        "use a categorical method instead"
    )


def has_defensible_numeric_representation(space: str) -> bool:
    """Whether arithmetic on the label means anything at all.

    ``ank``: yes, digits sit on a circle and 7 is 'larger' than 3 in an ordering
    sense, though not in a probabilistic sense - recorded as *weakly* meaningful.
    ``jodi``/``panna``: no. 47 is not more than 12, and 128 is not 128 units of
    anything.
    """
    return space == "ank"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# digit-level transforms (Category E)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def digital_root(value: int | str) -> int:
    """Repeated digit sum to a single digit (0 stays 0; 9 -> 9)."""
    total = sum(int(c) for c in str(value))
    while total > 9:
        total = sum(int(c) for c in str(total))
    return total


def digit_sum(value: int | str) -> int:
    return sum(int(c) for c in str(value))


def digit_complement(digit: int) -> int:
    """Decimal complement ``9 - d``."""
    return 9 - int(digit)


def reverse_string(value: str | int) -> str:
    """Reverse a fixed-width sequence, preserving width."""
    return str(value).strip()[::-1]


def hamming_distance(a: str, b: str) -> int:
    """Positional differences between two equal-length strings."""
    if len(a) != len(b):
        raise ValidationError(f"hamming distance needs equal lengths: {a!r} vs {b!r}")
    return sum(1 for x, y in zip(a, b, strict=True) if x != y)


def parity(value: int) -> int:
    return int(value) % 2


def residue(value: int, modulus: int) -> int:
    if modulus <= 0:
        raise ValidationError("modulus must be positive")
    return int(value) % modulus


def digit_sum_series(series: Iterable[str]) -> list[int]:
    return [digit_sum(v) for v in series]


def rot_class(ank: int, modulus: int = 10) -> int:
    """Residue class of the ank - used by the modular-arithmetic methods."""
    return int(ank) % modulus


### `src/preprocessing/quality_checks.py`

"""Data-quality gates.

These run before any analysis and their output is written to ``data_quality``.
A market with a failing ``error``-severity check is excluded from modelling:
producing a beautiful backtest on a corrupted table is worse than producing
nothing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import pandas as pd

from src.core.configuration import Config
from src.core.logging import get_logger
from src.core.validation import QualityReport, find_duplicate_dates, validate_chronology
from src.preprocessing.cleaning import clean_results
from src.storage.market_database import MarketDatabase

log = get_logger(__name__)


def run_quality_checks(config: Config, market_id: str, *, persist: bool = True) -> QualityReport:
    db = MarketDatabase(config, market_id)
    market = config.market(market_id)
    report = QualityReport(market_id=market.market_id)

    df = db.results()
    report.n_records = len(df)

    report.add("has_records", len(df) > 0, "n_records", len(df), severity="error",
               detail="an empty table cannot support any method")

    if df.empty:
        if persist:
            db.record_quality(report.to_rows())
        return report

    dates = df["result_date"].dt.normalize()
    report.add("unique_dates", dates.nunique() == len(dates), "duplicate_dates",
               find_duplicate_dates(dates.tolist()), severity="error")
    report.add("chronological_order", validate_chronology(dates.tolist()),
               "monotonic", bool(validate_chronology(dates.tolist())), severity="error")

    # Value-domain checks against the declared outcome space.
    for column, space, low, high in (("open_ank", "ank", 0, 9), ("close_ank", "ank", 0, 9)):
        if column not in df or df[column].isna().all():
            continue
        vals = df[column].dropna()
        ok = bool(vals.between(low, high).all())
        report.add(f"{column}_domain", ok, "n_out_of_range", int((~vals.between(low, high)).sum()),
                   severity="error")
        report.add(f"{column}_nulls", df[column].notna().all(), "n_missing",
                   int(df[column].isna().sum()), severity="warning")

    # Leading-zero preservation: jodi must always be two characters.
    if "jodi" in df:
        jodi = df["jodi"].dropna().astype(str)
        bad_width = int((jodi.str.len() != 2).sum())
        report.add("jodi_fixed_width", bad_width == 0, "n_bad_width", bad_width,
                   severity="error", detail="leading zeros must survive storage")
        leading_zero_rows = int(jodi.str.startswith("0").sum())
        report.add("jodi_leading_zeros_present", True, "n_leading_zero_values",
                   leading_zero_rows, severity="info",
                   detail="count of stored jodi values beginning with 0 (a good sign if > 0)")

    # Panna/ank arithmetic consistency.
    if {"open_panna", "open_ank"} <= set(df.columns):
        sub = df.dropna(subset=["open_panna", "open_ank"])
        if not sub.empty:
            derived = sub["open_panna"].map(lambda p: sum(int(c) for c in p) % 10)
            bad = int((derived != sub["open_ank"]).sum())
            report.add("open_panna_ank_consistent", bad == 0, "n_mismatch", bad,
                       severity="warning")

    # Coverage / gaps - reported, not "fixed".
    span_days = int((dates.max() - dates.min()).days) + 1
    missing = span_days - dates.nunique()
    report.add("coverage_reported", True, "missing_calendar_days", missing, severity="info",
               detail=f"{dates.nunique()} observed of {span_days} calendar days")
    coverage_pct = round(100 * dates.nunique() / max(span_days, 1), 2)
    report.add("coverage_threshold", coverage_pct >= 50.0, "coverage_pct", coverage_pct,
               severity="warning",
               detail="very sparse coverage weakens every chronological method")

    # Provenance.
    has_url = df["source_url"].notna()
    if config.dataset.is_live:
        report.add("source_url_present", bool(has_url.all()), "n_missing_url",
                   int((~has_url).sum()), severity="error",
                   detail="every live record must cite its source URL")
        bad_status = df["verification_status"].astype(str).str.startswith("synthetic")
        report.add("no_synthetic_rows_in_live", not bool(bad_status.any()),
                   "n_synthetic_rows", int(bad_status.sum()), severity="error")
    else:
        synthetic = df["verification_status"].astype(str).str.startswith("synthetic")
        report.add("synthetic_status_declared", bool(synthetic.all()),
                   "n_non_synthetic", int((~synthetic).sum()), severity="error",
                   detail="control datasets must be unmistakable in every row")

    # Revision audit trail.
    revisions = db.revision_log()
    report.add("revision_audit", True, "n_revisions", len(revisions), severity="info")

    # Duplicate-jodi-value sanity: not an error, but worth surfacing that the
    # ank marginal should be roughly flat if the draw is fair.
    for column in ("open_ank", "close_ank"):
        if column in df and df[column].notna().sum() > 100:
            counts = df[column].dropna().value_counts()
            ratio = float(counts.max() / max(counts.min(), 1))
            report.add(f"{column}_marginal_flatness", ratio < 3.0, "max_min_ratio", round(ratio, 3),
                       severity="info", detail="large imbalance would suggest a parsing error")

    if persist:
        db.record_quality(report.to_rows())
    log.info("quality %s: %d checks, %d errors, %d warnings",
             market_id, len(report.issues), len(report.errors), len(report.warnings))
    return report


def gate(config: Config, market_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Hard gate used by the modelling pipeline."""
    report = run_quality_checks(config, market_id)
    return {
        "market_id": market_id,
        "ok": report.ok,
        "n_records": report.n_records,
        "errors": [i.check for i in report.errors],
        "warnings": [i.check for i in report.warnings],
    }


### `src/preprocessing/psychology.py`

"""Player-psychology proxies derived from published history.

These features model what players *bet on* - not what will happen. They are
side-channel proxies for three documented biases:

* **availability / hot hand**: recent winners attract attention and money, so
  recent frequency is a proxy for where the public is looking;
* **gambler's fallacy**: numbers that have not appeared for a while are
  believed to be "due", so the gap since each ank last appeared proxies the
  pressure to bet on it;
* **engagement / coverage**: how many distinct anks the recent window has
  touched - a crude measure of how "alive" the market feels to players.

A jodi channel (open and close combined) is provided separately because the
jodi needs both series. Nothing here is claimed to predict the next draw: the
channel is a *description of public attention*, and whether attention moves
the result is an empirical question the backtest answers.

All features are causal: row ``t`` is computed from draws strictly before
``t``, exactly like the main feature matrix.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import warnings
from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

K_ANK = 10
_JODI = 100
_GAP_CAP = 999.0


@dataclass
class PsychologyConfig:
    """Knobs for the psychology channel. Defaults are deliberately compact."""

    heat_windows: tuple[int, ...] = (30, 90)
    include_momentum: bool = True
    include_cold_streak: bool = True
    include_coverage: bool = True
    include_jodi_heat: bool = True
    feature_version: str = "psych-v1"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ank-level channel (usable inside build_features)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _rolling_freq(y: np.ndarray, k: int, window: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Causal rolling frequency; row ``t`` uses the last ``window`` draws."""
    n = len(y)
    out = np.full((n, k), np.nan)
    counts = np.zeros(k)
    for t in range(n):
        total = counts.sum()
        if total > 0:
            out[t] = counts / total
        if y[t] >= 0:
            counts[y[t]] += 1
            if t - window >= 0 and y[t - window] >= 0:
                counts[y[t - window]] -= 1
    return out


def _gap_since_last(y: np.ndarray, k: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Draws elapsed since each ank was last seen (capped at 999)."""
    n = len(y)
    last_seen = np.full(k, -1)
    out = np.full((n, k), np.nan)
    for t in range(n):
        for c in range(k):
            out[t, c] = _GAP_CAP if last_seen[c] < 0 else float(t - last_seen[c])
        if y[t] >= 0:
            last_seen[y[t]] = t
    return out


def psychology_features(y_shifted: np.ndarray, cfg: PsychologyConfig) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Build the ank-level psychology channel from a *shifted* history.

    ``y_shifted`` follows the main feature matrix convention: row ``t`` holds
    the outcome of draw ``t-1`` (with ``-1`` as the warm-up sentinel), so row
    ``t`` describes the world a bettor would have seen before draw ``t``.
    """
    y = np.asarray(y_shifted, dtype=int)
    n = len(y)
    cols: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}

    heat = {}
    for w in cfg.heat_windows:
        heat[w] = _rolling_freq(y, K_ANK, w)
        for c in range(K_ANK):
            cols[f"heat_w{w}_{c}"] = heat[w][:, c] - 1.0 / K_ANK

    if cfg.include_momentum and len(cfg.heat_windows) >= 2:
        small, large = cfg.heat_windows[0], cfg.heat_windows[-1]
        for c in range(K_ANK):
            cols[f"heat_mom_{c}"] = heat[small][:, c] - heat[large][:, c]
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
            cols["heat_concentration"] = np.nanmax(
                heat[small] - 1.0 / K_ANK, axis=1)

    if cfg.include_cold_streak:
        gaps = _gap_since_last(y, K_ANK)
        expected = np.arange(1, n + 1, dtype=float) / K_ANK  # draws per ank so far
        expected = np.maximum(expected, 1.0)
        gaps_nn = np.nan_to_num(gaps, nan=0.0)
        cols["cold_max_norm"] = np.nanmax(gaps, axis=1) / expected
        cols["overdue_count"] = np.sum(
            np.maximum(gaps_nn - 1.5 * expected[:, None], 0) > 0, axis=1).astype(float)

    if cfg.include_coverage:
        for w in cfg.heat_windows:
            freq = _rolling_freq(y, K_ANK, w)
            cols[f"coverage_w{w}"] = np.sum(freq > 0, axis=1) / K_ANK

    frame = pd.DataFrame(cols)
    return frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# jodi-level channel (needs both the open and the close series)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _jodi_rolling_freq(seq: np.ndarray, window: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Rolling frequency of each of the 100 jodis; ``-1`` entries are ignored."""
    n = len(seq)
    out = np.full((n, _JODI), np.nan)
    counts = np.zeros(_JODI)
    for t in range(n):
        total = counts.sum()
        if total > 0:
            out[t] = counts / total
        j = seq[t]
        if 0 <= j < _JODI:
            counts[j] += 1
            if t - window >= 0 and 0 <= seq[t - window] < _JODI:
                counts[seq[t - window]] -= 1
    return out


def jodi_psychology_features(open_shifted: np.ndarray, close_shifted: np.ndarray,
                             cfg: PsychologyConfig) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Jodi-level heat channel. ``open_shifted``/``close_shifted`` are aligned.

    The jodi is formed exactly as the market forms it: open digit followed by
    close digit (open ``5`` + close ``1`` -> jodi ``51``).
    """
    o = np.asarray(open_shifted, dtype=int)
    c = np.asarray(close_shifted, dtype=int)
    valid = (o >= 0) & (c >= 0)
    j = np.where(valid, o * 10 + c, -1)
    n = len(j)
    cols: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}

    for w in cfg.heat_windows:
        freq = _jodi_rolling_freq(j, w)
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
            cols[f"jodi_heat_w{w}_top1"] = np.nanmax(freq - 1.0 / _JODI, axis=1)
        freq_nn = np.nan_to_num(freq, nan=0.0)
        cols[f"jodi_heat_w{w}_top1_id"] = np.argmax(freq_nn, axis=1).astype(float)

    # repetition pressure: how often the last window repeats the previous one
    if cfg.include_jodi_heat and len(cfg.heat_windows) >= 1:
        w = cfg.heat_windows[0]
        freq = _jodi_rolling_freq(j, w)
        recent = np.where(freq > 0, 1, 0)
        prior = np.roll(recent, 1, axis=0)
        prior[0] = 0
        both = np.sum(recent * prior, axis=1)
        total = np.sum(recent, axis=1)
        cols["jodi_repeat_rate"] = np.where(total > 0, both / np.maximum(total, 1), np.nan)

    frame = pd.DataFrame(cols)
    return frame.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

## Mathematics (100-Method Framework)

### `src/mathematics/types.py`

"""Shared types for the 100-method research framework.

A *method* is a documented statistical procedure plus an executable
implementation. The framework's contract with every method is:

* it receives a :class:`MethodContext` containing only validated, cleaned data
  and the resolved research parameters;
* it returns a :class:`MethodOutput` carrying real computed numbers, the sample
  size those numbers came from, and a plain-language interpretation;
* if the data cannot support the method, it says so via ``status`` rather than
  emitting a fabricated number.

``status`` values are deliberately narrow so the report can count them exactly.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Callable

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd


STATUS_COMPUTED = "computed"
STATUS_NOT_APPLICABLE = "not_applicable"
STATUS_INSUFFICIENT_DATA = "insufficient_data"
STATUS_UNAVAILABLE = "dependency_unavailable"
STATUS_FAILED = "failed"


@dataclass
class MethodContext:
    """Everything a method is allowed to see."""

    config: Any                       # resolved Config
    market_id: str
    market: Any                       # MarketSpec
    target: str                       # 'open' | 'close'
    space: str                        # 'ank' | 'jodi' | 'panna'
    k: int                            # size of the outcome space
    y: np.ndarray                     # integer-coded outcomes, chronological
    labels: list[str]                 # label for each code
    dates: pd.DatetimeIndex
    results: pd.DataFrame             # cleaned result table (active rows)
    series: pd.Series                 # date-indexed outcome series
    params: dict[str, Any]            # research.yaml 'methods' section
    seed: int
    dataset: str
    features: pd.DataFrame | None = None   # causal feature frame for this target
    model_panel: Any = None                # lazily built WalkForwardPanel
    extras: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    @property
    def n(self) -> int:
        return len(self.y)

    def rng(self, offset: int = 0) -> np.random.Generator:
        """Deterministic per-method generator so results reproduce exactly."""
        return np.random.default_rng(self.seed + offset)

    def label(self, code: int) -> str:
        if 0 <= code < len(self.labels):
            return self.labels[code]
        return str(code)

    def describe(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "market": self.market_id, "target": self.target, "space": self.space,
            "k": self.k, "n": self.n, "dataset": self.dataset,
            "first_date": str(self.dates[0].date()) if self.n else None,
            "last_date": str(self.dates[-1].date()) if self.n else None,
        }


@dataclass
class Finding:
    """One number, with the sample size that produced it."""

    metric_name: str
    metric_value: float | None
    statistic: float | None = None
    p_value: float | None = None
    effect_size: float | None = None
    sample_size: int | None = None
    extra: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def as_row(self, method: "MethodSpec", ctx: MethodContext | None,
               scope: str = "full_sample") -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "method_id": method.id,
            "method_name": method.name,
            "category": method.category,
            "market_id": ctx.market_id if ctx else None,
            "target": ctx.target if ctx else None,
            "scope": scope,
            "metric_name": self.metric_name,
            "metric_value": self.metric_value,
            "statistic": self.statistic,
            "p_value": self.p_value,
            "effect_size": self.effect_size,
            "sample_size": self.sample_size if self.sample_size is not None
            else (ctx.n if ctx else None),
            "extra": self.extra or None,
        }


@dataclass
class MethodOutput:
    status: str
    findings: list[Finding] = field(default_factory=list)
    narrative: str = ""
    walk_forward: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    diagnostics: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    @property
    def ok(self) -> bool:
        return self.status == STATUS_COMPUTED


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MethodSpec:
    """Documentation record for one of the 100 methods."""

    id: str
    name: str
    category: str
    formula: str
    theory: str
    objective: str
    assumptions: tuple[str, ...]
    variables: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]
    steps: tuple[str, ...]
    limitations: str
    data_requirements: str
    implementation: str
    references: str = ""

    @property
    def number(self) -> int:
        return int(self.id[1:])

    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "id": self.id, "name": self.name, "category": self.category,
            "formula": self.formula, "theory": self.theory, "objective": self.objective,
            "assumptions": list(self.assumptions),
            "variables": [{"symbol": s, "meaning": m} for s, m in self.variables],
            "steps": list(self.steps), "limitations": self.limitations,
            "data_requirements": self.data_requirements,
            "implementation": self.implementation, "references": self.references,
        }


Runner = Callable[[MethodContext], MethodOutput]


def finding(metric_name: str, metric_value: float | None, **kwargs: Any) -> Finding:
    """Convenience constructor that also sanitises numpy scalars."""
    def _f(v: Any) -> Any:
        if v is None:
            return None
        if isinstance(v, (np.floating, np.integer)):
            v = v.item()
        if isinstance(v, float) and (v != v or v in (float("inf"), float("-inf"))):
            return None
        return v

    return Finding(
        metric_name=metric_name, metric_value=_f(metric_value),
        statistic=_f(kwargs.get("statistic")), p_value=_f(kwargs.get("p_value")),
        effect_size=_f(kwargs.get("effect_size")),
        sample_size=kwargs.get("sample_size"), extra=kwargs.get("extra", {}),
    )


def note(condition: bool, text: str) -> str:
    return f"{'[yes]' if condition else '[no]'} {text}"


### `src/mathematics/registry.py`

"""The method registry: documentation + implementation, joined and validated.

The registry is the single source of truth for what the 100 methods are. Import
time validates that every documented method has an executable runner and that
every runner corresponds to a documented method - so a typo cannot silently drop
a method from the report.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Callable

from src.core.logging import get_logger
from src.mathematics import (
    advanced_statistics,
    frequency,
    machine_learning,
    markov,
    number_theory,
    randomness,
    recurrence,
    time_series,
)
from src.mathematics.catalog_ab import METHODS_AB
from src.mathematics.catalog_cd import METHODS_CD
from src.mathematics.catalog_ef import METHODS_EF
from src.mathematics.catalog_gh import METHODS_GH
from src.mathematics.types import MethodOutput, MethodSpec

log = get_logger(__name__)

CATEGORY_NAMES = {
    "A": "Frequency and Probability",
    "B": "Recency and Occurrence",
    "C": "Transitions and Dependencies",
    "D": "Time Series",
    "E": "Number Theory and Transformations",
    "F": "Randomness and Statistical Structure",
    "G": "Machine Learning",
    "H": "Advanced Probability, Ensembles and Validation",
}

_MODULES = {
    "src.mathematics.frequency": frequency,
    "src.mathematics.recurrence": recurrence,
    "src.mathematics.markov": markov,
    "src.mathematics.time_series": time_series,
    "src.mathematics.number_theory": number_theory,
    "src.mathematics.randomness": randomness,
    "src.mathematics.machine_learning": machine_learning,
    "src.mathematics.advanced_statistics": advanced_statistics,
}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RegisteredMethod:
    spec: MethodSpec
    runner: Callable

    @property
    def id(self) -> str:
        return self.spec.id

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        return self.spec.name

    @property
    def category(self) -> str:
        return self.spec.category

    def run(self, ctx) -> MethodOutput:
        return self.runner(ctx)


def _build_registry() -> dict[str, RegisteredMethod]:
    specs = {m.id: m for m in (METHODS_AB + METHODS_CD + METHODS_EF + METHODS_GH)}
    registry: dict[str, RegisteredMethod] = {}
    for method_id, spec in specs.items():
        module_name, func_name = spec.implementation.split("::")
        module = _MODULES.get(module_name)
        if module is None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{method_id}: unknown implementation module '{module_name}'")
        runner = getattr(module, func_name, None)
        if runner is None:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{method_id}: '{func_name}' not found in {module_name}")
        registry[method_id] = RegisteredMethod(spec=spec, runner=runner)
    return registry


METHOD_REGISTRY: dict[str, RegisteredMethod] = _build_registry()

#: Methods 91 and 92 are meta-analyses and must run last.
META_METHODS = ["M091", "M092"]
ORDERED_METHOD_IDS = [f"M{i:03d}" for i in range(1, 101)]


def get(method_id: str) -> RegisteredMethod:
    if method_id not in METHOD_REGISTRY:
        raise KeyError(f"unknown method '{method_id}'")
